match.reason: No bank point teaches using a straight-line model to make predictions and the limits of extrapolation: linear functions covers gradients and parallel lines, and modelling with functions is a Year 12 point about choosing between model types.

draft.title: Linear models
card: A linear model uses a straight-line equation to describe how two quantities are related. It is written y = mx + c, where m is the rate of change and c is the starting amount.

To predict, put a value of x into the equation and work out y. Example: a taxi charges C = 3 + 2d, where C is the cost in dollars and d is the distance in km. For 10 km, C = 3 + 2 × 10 = 23, so the cost is $23.
To find x from a known y, put y into the equation and solve. If C = 17, then 17 = 3 + 2d, so 2d = 14 and d = 7 km.

A model is only built from real data in a certain range. Predicting outside that range is extrapolation, and the model may stop being accurate there, because the real pattern may not stay a straight line.
draft.remember: Put x in to predict y, but be careful of predictions outside the data the model came from.

a.q: A plumber's charge is C = 60 + 45h, where C is the cost in dollars and h is the hours worked. What is the cost of a 3 hour job?
a.why: C = 60 + 45 × 3 = 60 + 135 = 195, so the cost is $195. The answer $135 leaves out the $60 call-out fee, and $108 comes from adding 60 + 45 and then multiplying by 3 incorrectly.
a.clue: Multiply first, then add the starting amount.

b.q: Sam's plant height model is H = 5 + 2t, where H is height in cm and t is days. It was made from data for days 1 to 10. Which prediction is least reliable?
b.why: Day 60 is far outside the data from days 1 to 10, so it is extrapolation and the plant may not keep growing at the same rate. Days 4, 9 and 10 are inside the range the model was built from, so they are more reliable.
b.clue: Which day is furthest from the data used to make the model?

problems.detail: The why says $108 comes from adding 60 + 45 and then multiplying by 3. That gives (60 + 45) × 3 = $315, not $108. $108 actually comes from adding all three numbers: 60 + 45 + 3. The explanation of this distractor is wrong and would confuse a student checking their error.

check.summary: Both questions have the right answers ($195 and day 60). The explanation for question a wrongly says $108 comes from (60 + 45) × 3, when it actually comes from 60 + 45 + 3.
